title: When the Vow Wakes
premise: Quentin Halloran, once a celebrated wedding planner who fled the industry after a scandal destroyed his reputation and his engagement, now runs a quiet vineyard inn and volunteers for a prison pen-pal program that promises anonymity. The letters he receives from 'Inmate 4471' are sharp, funny, and unsettlingly perceptive—until he learns the writer is Marisol Vega, the investigative journalist whose exposé ruined him a decade ago and who is now serving time for refusing to reveal a source. Forced into a mediated reconciliation by the program's rules, Quentin and Marisol must decide whether the truth that destroyed them can be the thing that finally frees them, culminating in a public reckoning at the vineyard's first harvest festival where Quentin chooses to testify, Marisol chooses to stay, and both risk the whole heart instead of lending pieces.
about_author: F. M. Delacroix is the pen name of a former hospitality insider who spent fifteen years orchestrating other people's happiest days before turning to fiction. They write stories about people who rebuild themselves in the spaces between what was taken and what remains.

chapters.title: Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Ten years after fleeing the wedding industry in disgrace, Quentin measures his life in careful increments—the vineyard inn, the anonymous pen-pal volunteer work, the weddings he refuses to plan. When the program assigns him Inmate 4471, he writes a polite, distant first letter. Emotional beat: the ache of a man who has mistaken safety for peace.

chapters.title: The Sharpest Pen
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Inside Alder Creek Correctional, journalist Marisol Vega recognizes the handwriting style of the pen-pal assignment before the name arrives: Quentin Halloran, the man her exposé unmade. She almost requests a reassignment, then chooses to write honestly instead of apologetically. Emotional beat: defiant curiosity—she'd rather be hated truthfully than liked through a lie.

chapters.title: Correspondence War
chapters.summary: Alternating POV via letters. Their exchange becomes a duel: Marisol defends her exposé's accuracy; Quentin catalogs the wreckage it left—his engagement, his business, his name. But her questions are precise, and his answers surprise them both. Emotional beat: the dangerous intimacy of enemies who can't stop writing.

chapters.title: What the Source Cost
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Flashbacks reveal why Marisol sits in prison: she refused to name the whistleblower behind her story about Halloran's former firm, choosing contempt over complicity. Quentin's letters begin to crack her certainty that the story was worth it. Emotional beat: the first tremor of doubt about a sacrifice she called justice.

chapters.title: The Program Has Rules
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The program coordinator reveals the pairing wasn't random—a board member arranged it, hoping the publicity will save the program from budget cuts. Quentin feels used, and worse, realizes he doesn't want the letters to end. He writes to Marisol anyway, breaking his own rule of distance. Emotional beat: choosing connection despite manipulation.

chapters.title: Visiting Hours
chapters.summary: Both POV, alternating scenes. Quentin visits in person for the first time; the glass between them is thinner than the page ever was. They argue, laugh, and nearly say too much. Marisol asks him to look into the source she protected—a person whose safety she traded her life for. Emotional beat: the vow of old loyalty tested by new feeling.

chapters.title: The Whistleblower's Name
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Following Marisol's clues, Quentin discovers the source was his former business partner, Daniel, who leaked the records to protect workers—and who has since vanished, possibly threatened by the firm's owners. The truth reframes everything: Marisol's story was right; the punishment was wrong. Emotional beat: grief and fury braided together.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol is released early on a technicality just as the vineyard's first harvest begins. She arrives unannounced, and the reunion is raw—gratitude tangled with resentment, tenderness with fear. Daniel resurfaces, terrified, asking Marisol to stay silent again. Emotional beat: the cost of justice made flesh, standing in her doorway.

chapters.title: The Testimony
chapters.summary: Both POV, converging. At the harvest festival, with press present, Quentin publicly tells his own story—refusing the victim narrative, vindicating Marisol, and naming the firm's retaliation against Daniel. Marisol chooses to reopen the investigation, risking her freedom again. Daniel agrees to come forward. Emotional beat: the climax—both risk the whole heart, in public, together.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, epilogue-style. Months later: the firm's executives are indicted, Daniel is safe, and Marisol's story runs with her byline restored. Quentin plans one wedding—their own, small, in the vineyard, among the vines that finally came in. Emotional beat: quiet, earned joy; identity rebuilt not in spite of memory but with it.
